reason: The hypothesis directly restates the finding of P3 and P5 that Y and Hf co-doping improves thermal stability and hot corrosion scale spallation in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA coatings, and applies it to a generic HEA bond coat for TBCs. The mechanism is taken from P13's explanation of grain boundary pinning by reactive elements. The proposal is essentially the same intervention on the same material class, with no new alloy system, mechanism, or integration of conflicting evidence.
copied_elements: reactive element addition (Y, Hf) to HEA bond coat
improved thermal stability and scale spallation resistance
mechanism: reactive element segregation at grain boundaries retards grain growth
predicted outcome: more uniform, adherent, slow-growing TGO
